label: Continued the Mesoamerican-Andean testimonial tradition against dispossession
description: Following the lineage of colonial Indigenous chronicles like Guaman Poma's appeal to imperial conscience, Menchú's I, Rigoberta Menchú deployed testimonial narrative on a global stage to bear collective witness to Mayan genocide.
dialecticalTension: Transforms historical chronicle into contemporary global human-rights testimonio.
historicalContext: Longue-durée Indigenous testimonial tradition in Latin America.

citations.author: John Beverley
citations.work: Testimonio: On the Politics of Truth

label: Embodied critical consciousness and collective narrative praxis (testimonio)
description: Menchú's testimonial philosophy operationalized Freirean conscientization by speaking in the first-person plural of K'iche' Maya community survival, triggering widespread philosophical debate on collective truth.
dialecticalTension: Challenges Western individualistic verification models with communal testimonial truth.
historicalContext: Guatemalan civil conflict and liberation theology / popular education networks (1983).

label: Informed Latin American liberation ethics of the exteriorized Indigenous victim
description: Enrique Dussel's philosophy of liberation explicitly invoked Rigoberta Menchú's testimony as the concrete ethical voice of the marginalized Indigenous "Other" interrupting modern colonial totality.
dialecticalTension: Bridges Dussel's ethical exteriority with lived Maya ecological and civic resistance.
historicalContext: Ethics of Liberation (1998) and late-20th-century Indigenous human rights.

citations.author: Enrique Dussel
citations.work: Ethics of Liberation in the Age of Globalization and Exclusion
